entry_conditions: Either the fingers are still coupled to the observed lid handle near the open-lid boundary, or the lid has been released and the peg remains in the box. Two causal frames must be available across the switch.
exit_conditions: Closed fingers, peg above the box rim, and peg/TCP co-motion jointly indicate readiness; the policy may continue through initial turn up to the index-1270 boundary.
overlap_role: Explicit phase observables condition every supervised action in incoming [740,950) and outgoing [1120,1270), retaining robust early and late switches rather than narrowing supervision to the central grasp.
successor_readiness: reorient_and_stage_peg is ready when closed fingers, peg height above the wall, and low two-frame change of peg-to-TCP relation agree while peg and TCP move. This is guidance, not contact truth.
failure_signatures: Behavior returns toward the lid while open near the peg; premature closure; descent while still coupled to the handle; stationary peg during commanded lift; changing peg/TCP offset; wall-stalled motion; or persistent IK residual and joint-limit contacts.
continuation_guidance: Use this policy for early lid-held or phase-ambiguous entries. Prefer retrieve_peg_from_box__h01 after release when peg displacement dominates, and retrieve_peg_from_box__h02 when modest hand-configuration mismatch dominates. Never treat negative gripper command as proof of grasp.
limitations: Two-frame co-motion can be ambiguous while stationary, and all demonstrations are successful. World targets do not construct peg-displacement invariance, cannot guarantee reachability or collision avoidance, and do not cover drop or regrasp recovery.
